What would it need to earn?

These are hypothetical CAD assumptions. They are separate from the observed conversion rates.

Can I use this comparison?

The counts behind the rates

I keep users who never saw an ad and users with no purchase event. Filtering to exposed users would change the randomized comparison.

Check a group without choosing it from the final result

The table always compares the two predefined customer groups for the selected experiment, split and device. The customer filter above does not remove a row. The development choice used all devices. Device slices and other group views are exploratory, with unadjusted intervals. A group difference has not been established by these separate intervals.

Trace an example user

A fixed sample of up to 3 users from each experiment × split × customer type × device × arm cell. This is for tracing the calculation. It is not the full experiment or a representative sample for estimating lift.

How much data would a future test need?

Use a baseline and a minimum useful absolute increase. This is an approximate fixed-horizon calculation for equal allocation, 80% power and a two-sided 5% test.

The planning inputs are independent of the campaign filters. This does not estimate the probability that the current result is correct. Allow more users for clustering, unequal allocation, missing data or multiple primary outcomes. Avoid repeated early stopping.

How I calculated it

One user, one outcome

I remove identical assignment and event re-deliveries. Purchases count from assignment up to, but not including, 7 days later. A user with two purchases is still one converted user. All assigned users have a complete observation window.

Compare assignment, not exposure

The main estimate is treatment conversions / treatment users minus control conversions / control users. It is an intention-to-treat comparison. I do not remove non-exposed users.

Keep evaluation separate

The generator assigns 40% to development and 60% to evaluation independently of treatment and outcomes. I choose one customer group using the larger development lower interval bound. I then inspect that fixed group in evaluation. The overall evaluation comparison is the primary result. Other interactive slices are exploratory.

Check allocation first

The planned allocation is 50/50. A chi-square sample-ratio p-value below 0.001 or orphan conversion users blocks the full experiment. A filter cannot clear that block. Passing this check does not establish that every other assumption is valid.

Uncertainty and money

I use a 95% Newcombe interval built from Wilson score intervals for the two conversion rates. The contribution interval is the effect interval × contribution per conversion minus treatment cost, for 1,000 treated users. Contribution and cost are fixed hypothetical inputs. A follow-up rollout is supported only when the whole net interval is above zero. This is a scenario decision, not evidence of realized profit.

Data and limits

All 3 experiments are synthetic, with seed 89. The broken case omits control assignment records. A public Criteo extension was deferred because the download was unavailable. There is no live ad platform, attribution feed or model integration.
